correctness.rationale: The infinite proof splits N into r=1,2,3 coprime prime-power blocks. r=1 gives (M-1)N=2; r=2 gives M=2 then (A-1)(B-1)=3, whose sole candidate blocks (2,4) are not coprime; r=3 bounds sigma*/N <=12/5 and N>=30, hence M=2. The linear equation C(AB-A-B-1)=AB+A+B+2 forces (for A=2) B-3|13 with B=4 or16 noncoprime; for A=3 an even denominator divides 13, impossible; and for A>=4,B>=5, monotone D(A,B)=AB^2-2AB-B^2-2B-A-2>=19 forces C<B, contradicting order. An independent factorization enumeration of 2<=N<=40000 found only N=2. This finite check supplements, not proves, the unbounded case.
residual_risks: The conclusion does not bound support >=4 or establish existence of further solutions.
